Cooldowns, warmups and arrival effects are configured in each feature's own file. For example, in features/home.yml:
Each feature defines how it chooses a landing position.

Sparrow provides everyday administration commands, homes, warps, teleport requests, random teleportation and custom death messages for Paper and Folia. Use Commands and permissions as a quick reference. Feature pages cover usage and essential configuration; developers can start with the Teleport API.

File Contents config.yml Database, Redis and other base settings. server.yml This server's ID and tags. commands.yml Command entry points, switches and permissions; restart after editing. modules.yml Feature module switches. features/ Separate configuration files for each module. Use /spr feature_list to check module states. /spr feature_enable <module> and /spr feature_disable <module> change the current state without saving it. Edit modules.yml to keep your choice after a reload or restart. Run /spr reload after editing settings; its feedback identifies changes that need a restart. Cross-server features require shared database and Redis connections, plus the Sparrow companion plugin on the proxy. PlaceholderAPI is optional for text placeholders; LuckPerms provides permission lookups.

Add the current Sparrow build as a compile dependency and declare your plugin's dependency on Sparrow. Here, player is a local online SparrowPlayer, and logger is your plugin's logger. import java.util.logging.Level; import net.momirealms.sparrow.teleport.Teleport; import net.momirealms.sparrow.teleport.TeleportSubmission; import net.momirealms.sparrow.teleport.processor.post.PlaySound; TeleportSubmission submission = Teleport.builder() .server("lobby") .position("world", 0.5, 64, 0.5) .postProcessor(new PlaySound()) .commit(player) .onResult(result -> result.ifFail(fail -> player.sendTranslatedMessage(fail.reason()))) .onError(error -> logger.log(Level.SEVERE, "Teleport failed", error)); server takes a Sparrow server ID; the local ID uses a local teleport. Cross-server requests require configured Sparrow backends and proxy services. commit also accepts a Bukkit Player. Submit each builder once.

Expression Purpose position(world, x, y, z[, yaw, pitch]) Fixed coordinates. position(TeleportPosition.ofPos(worldLocation)) A saved WorldLocation. position(TeleportPosition.ofPlayer(uuid)) A player on the destination server; also accepts a player name. position(TeleportPosition.rtpBuilder()...build()) A random search within areas. server(...) also accepts Supplier<String> and CompletionStage<String>. Player destinations capture coordinates during preparation; they do not keep tracking movement. Fixed coordinates are used directly. Add FindSafeLoc for a safety check: FindSafeLoc safe = FindSafeLoc.builder() .search(SearchPattern.exact(), SearchPattern.nearby().horizontalRadius(4).up(8).down(8).build()) .rules(PhysicalSafety.builder().build()) .chunks(ChunkPolicy.EXISTING_ONLY) .maxChecks(10_000) .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3)) .build(); Teleport.builder() .server("survival") .position("world", 100.5, 64, 100.5) .targetProcessor(safe) .postProcessor(new Invulnerability(5)) .commit(player); SearchPattern provides exact(), nearby() and column(), tried in order. PhysicalSafety checks collisions, support, boundaries and hazards; it rejects water, leaf support and Nether-roof locations by default. EXISTING_ONLY uses generated chunks; ALLOW_GENERATION permits generation. For random teleportation, build a destination: TeleportPosition random = TeleportPosition.rtpBuilder() .areas(RtpArea.builder("world").rectangle(-5000, -5000, 5000, 5000).build()) .nearbyColumns(2, 4, 4) .rules(PhysicalSafety.builder().build()) .chunks(ChunkPolicy.ALLOW_GENERATION) .maxAttempts(32) .maxChecks(10_000) .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(9)) .build(); Teleport.builder().server("survival").position(random).commit(player); rectangle takes minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ, optionally followed by minY, maxY. Multiple areas may use different worlds on the same destination server. Available scan modes are AUTO, SURFACE, CAVITY_TOP_DOWN and CAVITY_BOTTOM_UP. The example sets the search ranges and budgets explicitly. targetProcessor checks or adjusts coordinates after destination resolution. A custom PositionProcessor returns Accept, Reject or Relocate. postProcessor runs actions in order after arrival; built-ins include PlaySound and Invulnerability.

Attach a condition to prepare the destination while waiting for confirmation or a countdown: CompletableFuture<Void> confirmation = new CompletableFuture<>(); TeleportSubmission pending = Teleport.builder() .server("lobby") .position("world", 0.5, 64, 0.5) .condition(confirmation) .commit(player); Call confirmation.complete(null) to confirm, or pending.cancel() to cancel. Execution waits for every condition to complete normally; a failed or cancelled condition produces Aborted. Only completion status matters: a CompletableFuture<Boolean> completed with false still passes. Entry point Meaning onPrepared(...) Preparation succeeded; exposes the destination without pausing execution. onResult(...) Success, Fail(reason) or Aborted(cause); use ifSuccess, ifFail and ifAborted to handle branches. onError(...) A program error. preparationResult() / result() Observation Futures for composition; do not complete or cancel them yourself. cancel() Cancels only before execution starts; returns true on cancellation and produces Fail(TELEPORT_CANCELLED). commitForget(player) Ignore business results and log program errors. Success reports the completed move without waiting for all post-processors. Callbacks have no player-thread guarantee; schedule entity or world mutations as required by the platform.

context(new TeleportContext()) carries NBT parameters and belongs to the request after submission. Setting TeleportContext.UNSAFE to true lets FindSafeLoc fall back to its input coordinates when the search fails. RTP does not use this fallback. Extension interface Type registry TeleportPosition TeleportPosition.TYPES PositionProcessor PositionProcessor.TYPES PostProcessor PostProcessor.TYPES SafetyRule SafetyRule.TYPES Implement type() and toNbt(), then register a decoder with the corresponding registry's register(type, decoder). Register on the sending server and every possible receiving server. Transfer configuration in NBT; obtain service objects locally. Put restrictions in SafetyRule when a search should continue trying candidates. RTP's testBeforeResolve can check X/Z early and return PASS, REJECT or DEFER; DEFER calls test after resolving Y. A later target processor's rejection does not restart RTP, and relocated coordinates are not rechecked against earlier area restrictions. TeleportRequestEvent and TeleportReadyEvent run on the destination server before resolution and after target processing; both are cancellable. TeleportArriveEvent exposes departure and arrival locations after a cross-server arrival.

<argument> is required; [argument] is optional. These are the default entry points and permissions. Short commands also accept /sparrow <command> or /spr <command>. Restart after editing commands.yml. [.other] marks branches that additionally require .other when specifying another player. Entity selectors only select local targets; commands with cross-server support also accept a player name from another backend.

Command Purpose Default permission /sparrow reload [--silent] Reload configuration. sparrow.command.admin.reload /sparrow feature_list [page] List module states. sparrow.command.admin.feature /sparrow feature_enable <feature> Enable a module immediately without saving its switch. sparrow.command.admin.feature /sparrow feature_disable <feature> Disable a module immediately without saving its switch. sparrow.command.admin.feature Use death_messages as the feature name to manage Death messages. Edit modules.yml to keep module switches after a reload or restart.

player.name selects another owner's home. sparrow.command.home[.other] /set_home [name] Create a home at your position; the default name is home. sparrow.command.set_home /del_home <name> Delete a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.del_home[.other] /home_list [owner|page] [page] List your homes or another owner's homes. sparrow.command.home_list[.other] /edit_home <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.edit_home[.other] /sparrow del_all_homes [--player <player>] [--server <server>] [--world <world>] Bulk delete from console; at least one filter, no confirmation. sparrow.command.del_all_homes /tpa <player> Ask to teleport to another player. sparrow.command.tpa /tpa_here <player> Ask another player to teleport to you. sparrow.command.tpa_here /tpa_accept [player] Accept a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_accept /tpa_deny [player] Deny a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_deny /tpa_cancel [player] Cancel an outgoing request; omit the player to cancel all. sparrow.command.tpa_cancel

ban_history accepts --page, --active, --within <duration> and --operator <name>; see Bans. rtp_range accepts --center-x, --center-z, --min-y, --max-y and --silent; see Random teleport. The rename and relocate branches of edit_home and edit_warp require .rename and .relocate appended to the base permission. Editing another owner's home also requires .other. item_lore operations are insert, remove, edit, up and down. Run it without options to open the editor panel. See Highlight for region, color and duration options. Messages and item text use MiniMessage. Use <papi:placeholder> or <papi:placeholder:default> for PlaceholderAPI. item_name, custom_name and item_lore accept JSON with --json.

Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.maintenance Allow entry during maintenance. sparrow.bypass.player_limit Allow entry when full. sparrow.bypass.patrol Exclude from patrol. sparrow.notify.ban Receive ban and unban notices. sparrow.bypass.tpa_cooldown Skip request and denial cooldowns. sparrow.home.limit.<amount> / sparrow.home.limit.unlimited Override the home limit. sparrow.warp.use.<lowercase-name> Allow access to a warp when permission-restrict is enabled. sparrow.back.staff / sparrow.back.vip Default Back cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.deathback.staff / sparrow.deathback.vip Default DeathBack cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.rtp.staff / sparrow.rtp.vip Default RTP cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.tpa.staff / sparrow.tpa.vip Default TPA teleport cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.home.teleport.staff / sparrow.home.teleport.vip Default Home cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.warp.teleport.staff / sparrow.warp.teleport.vip Default Warp cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.spawn.staff Default Spawn cooldown and warmup override. Teleport override permissions are configurable in each feature's teleport-options.overrides; RTP region permissions use regions.<name>.permission.

Module back · Configuration features/back.yaml /back returns to the previous departure point; /death-back returns to the last death location. Both support cross-server destinations. A named traveler must be on this server. Command Purpose Default permission /back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the previous teleport departure point. sparrow.command.back[.other] /death-back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the last death location. sparrow.command.death-back[.other] --unsafe allows the original coordinates when no safe location is found; --silent hides command feedback. back.teleport-causes records COMMAND and PLUGIN by default. back.join-grace-seconds ignores ordinary teleports during the first 3 seconds after joining. deathback.record-death controls recording of new death locations. Configure their cooldowns and warmups separately under back.teleport-options and deathback.teleport-options; see Teleport options.

Module ban · Configuration features/ban.yml Ban accounts, IPs or IP ranges across servers, with a persistent history. Command Purpose Default permission /ban <player|player_ip|ip> <target> [reason] [--time <duration>] [--force] [--silent] Ban an account or IP. sparrow.command.ban /unban <player|player_ip|ip> <target> [--silent] Lift an account or IP ban. sparrow.command.unban /unban_id <id> [--silent] Revoke a ban by record ID. sparrow.command.unban_id /ban_info <id> View a ban record. sparrow.command.ban_info /ban_history <all|player <player>|ip <ip>> [options] Search ban history. sparrow.command.ban_history /ban player Steve griefing --time 7d /ban player_ip Steve /ban ip 192.0.2.* unwanted traffic /ban_history player Steve --active /unban_id 12 player bans an account. player_ip bans the player's last recorded IP without adding an account ban. ip accepts an address or range. Omit --time for a permanent ban; --force replaces an active ban for the same target. --silent hides notices and success feedback. History filters are --page <page>, --active, --within <duration> and --operator <name>. sparrow.notify.ban receives ban and unban notices. Add common reasons to reason-presets; an exact preset name expands to its text. Notification sounds use notify-ban-sound and notify-unban-sound.

Module death_messages · Configuration features/death_messages.yml Customize player death announcements with complete sentences for each vanilla death situation. Messages support MiniMessage, player hover text and the weapon details supplied by Minecraft. Announcements can stay on the current server or be broadcast across the network. Minecraft's death attribution is preserved, including deaths while escaping an attacker and assisted falls. The death screen keeps its existing message. When death announcements are already hidden by the server or another plugin, Sparrow leaves them hidden.

The module is enabled by default. Its persistent switch is in modules.yml: death_messages: true Command Purpose Default permission /spr feature_enable death_messages Enable rewriting on this server immediately. sparrow.command.admin.feature /spr feature_disable death_messages Stop rewriting on this server immediately. sparrow.command.admin.feature /spr reload Apply configuration changes. sparrow.command.admin.reload The enable and disable commands change the current state without saving the switch. Edit modules.yml to keep the choice after a reload or restart. If the DeathMessages configuration is invalid, reloading fails for this module and its last valid settings remain active. There are no feature-specific commands or permissions. Disabling this module stops rewriting deaths that happen on this server; players may still receive cross-server announcements from other servers. See Commands and permissions for module management.

The generated file contains 101 default rules. The example below shows only a few rules and customized display text; edit the generated file to keep the other death situations covered. broadcast: false disabled_worlds: [] anti-spam: enabled: true interval: 30s max-messages: 3 show-to-victim: true format: '<dark_gray>☠ <gray><arg:message>' display: player: name: '<white><arg:display_name>' hover: - '<gray>Player: <white><arg:name>' - '<gray>Server: <white><arg:server>' mob: name: '<yellow><arg:entity_name>' fallback: - '<arg:original>' rules: - id: player_with_weapon message_key: death.attack.player.item broadcast: true messages: - '<arg:attacker> killed <arg:victim> using <arg:weapon>' - '<arg:victim> was defeated by <arg:attacker> using <arg:weapon>' - id: lava_escape message_key: death.attack.lava.player messages: - '<arg:victim> jumped into lava while escaping <arg:attacker>' - id: ladder_fall message_key: death.fell.accident.ladder messages: - '<arg:victim> fell off a ladder'

Field Meaning id A nonempty, unique name for the rule. message_key The exact vanilla death-message key, including capitalization and any suffix. broadcast Optional override for the public broadcast setting. disabled_worlds Optional replacement for the public disabled-world list. messages Required list of complete sentences. One entry is selected randomly for each death. If several rules have the same message_key, the first one wins. Keys are matched exactly: a rule for death.attack.player does not also match death.attack.player.item. All recipients share the same randomly selected sentence. Each sentence can place the victim, attacker and weapon wherever you want. messages: [] hides that death situation, including the outer format. A selected empty string also hides the announcement. A rule that hides an announcement does not continue to another rule or use fallback. Unmatched keys use a random entry from fallback, together with the public broadcast and disabled_worlds settings. The default fallback, <arg:original>, keeps the vanilla death message inside your outer format. Set fallback: [] to hide unmatched situations. Some useful vanilla keys are: message_key Situation death.attack.player Killed by a player. death.attack.player.item Killed by a player, with weapon details supplied by Minecraft. death.attack.mob Killed by a mob. death.attack.arrow.item Shot, with weapon details supplied by Minecraft. death.attack.lava Died in lava. death.attack.lava.player Died in lava while escaping an attacker. death.fell.accident.ladder Fell off a ladder. death.fell.assist.item An attacker caused a fatal fall, with weapon details. death.fell.finish Fell and was finished off by an attacker. death.attack.badRespawnPoint.message A bed or respawn-anchor explosion, with the vanilla death-reason link. The .player suffix is part of Minecraft's key naming; the attributed attacker can also be a mob. Use the generated rules as the reference for the remaining keys.

Public setting Default Meaning broadcast false false announces locally; true announces across the Sparrow network. disabled_worlds [] Hide deaths occurring in these worlds. Names are matched exactly on the server where the death occurs. A rule inherits either setting when it omits that field. An explicit value replaces the public value: broadcast: false overrides a public broadcast: true; false still announces locally. disabled_worlds: [] clears the disabled-world restriction for that rule. A nonempty rule list replaces the public world list completely; the lists are not merged. For example, this configuration normally broadcasts across the network and hides deaths in lobby. The weapon rule announces locally and also permits announcements for deaths in lobby: broadcast: true disabled_worlds: [lobby] rules: - id: local_weapon_kill message_key: death.attack.player.item broadcast: false disabled_worlds: [] messages: - '<arg:victim> was killed by <arg:attacker> using <arg:weapon>' These choices come from the server where the death occurs. A disabled world hides that announcement for everyone, including players on other servers; it does not filter recipients by their current world. Receiving servers use the selected announcement and do not choose another rule or sentence. For cross-server announcements, use Sparrow versions that support this feature on the receiving backends and configure the network as described in the Introduction. Player and weapon hover details are retained across servers.

Setting Purpose format Outer chat format. <arg:message> inserts the selected sentence. display.player.name Display format shared by the victim and player attackers. display.player.hover Lines shown when hovering over a displayed player. [] adds no custom hover text. display.mob.name Mob name display. <arg:entity_name> preserves custom names and vanilla translated names. Use these arguments in rule messages, fallback text and the outer format: Argument Value <arg:victim> The victim, with the configured player display. <arg:attacker> The attacker attributed by Minecraft, with the configured player or mob display. Available only in applicable situations. <arg:weapon> The weapon name and item hover supplied by the vanilla message. Available only in applicable .item situations. <arg:death_reason> The special reason link for a bed or respawn-anchor explosion. <arg:original> The complete vanilla death message, with its original names and hover details. <arg:server> The ID of the server where the death occurred. <arg:world> The name of the world where the death occurred. <arg:x>, <arg:y>, <arg:z> Death location as block coordinates. <arg:message_key> The vanilla key selected for this death. attacker, weapon and death_reason are not available for every death. Use them in matching rules, or supply a default such as <arg:weapon:'unknown weapon'> in a shared template. Weapon availability follows Minecraft's death message; holding a weapon does not guarantee that the message supplies it. All default .item rules include <arg:weapon>. Inside display.player, <arg:name> is that player's account name and <arg:display_name> is their display name. <arg:server> remains the server where the death occurred. PlaceholderAPI is optional. With it installed, use <papi:placeholder> or <papi:placeholder:default>, rather than %placeholder%: In display.player.name and display.player.hover, PAPI refers to the displayed player: the victim for their name, or the player attacker for theirs. In messages, fallback and format, PAPI refers to each recipient. For example, <papi:player_name> shows the viewer's name, including on another server. Mob display text has no player-specific PAPI context.

Setting Default Meaning anti-spam.enabled true Limit repeated announcements from the same player. anti-spam.interval 30s Positive duration with units, such as 30s or 1m. anti-spam.max-messages 3 Positive maximum number of normal announcements in that interval. anti-spam.show-to-victim true Send excess announcements only to the victim. false hides them from everyone. With the defaults, the first three announcements from a player within the preceding 30 seconds are sent normally. Further deaths in that window are shown only to that player and are not broadcast across servers. Excess deaths still count, so continued deaths can keep the limit active until older deaths leave the window. Deaths hidden by the server, another plugin, a disabled-world rule or an empty message do not count. show-to-victim does not override those hiding rules. Limits apply separately on each server and reset when the player leaves that server or the module is disabled.

Module head · Configuration features/head.yml Get a head from a player name or UUID. Omit the source to get your own head. Command Purpose Default permission /head [source] [amount] [player] [--force] [--silent] Obtain a player head. sparrow.command.head[.other] /head Notch /head Notch 16 Steve --force Amounts range from 1 to 6400. --force refreshes profile data. By default, Sparrow tries online player textures before the API. Source order, cache settings and endpoints are configurable.

Module highlight · Configuration features/highlight.yml Show block outlines to selected viewers without changing real blocks. Omitting targets shows them to online players in that world. Command Purpose Default permission /highlight [targets] [options] Highlight a region's blocks. sparrow.command.highlight /highlight @s --from 0 64 0 --to 5 68 5 --highlight-color green --highlight-duration 20 Without coordinates, select two points interactively: left-click records your position; right-click records the clicked block. Run the command again without coordinates to cancel selection. Option Purpose --from, --to Endpoints; provide both. --world <world> World; required from console. --highlight-duration <seconds> / -d Duration from 0 to 300 seconds. --highlight-color <color> / -c A named color, such as green or red. --solid-only Show solid blocks exposed to passable neighbors or the selection boundary. --silent / -s Hide command feedback. Defaults are 30 seconds of display, a 32768-block limit and a 30-second selection timeout. Peaceful worlds are not supported.

Module home · Configuration features/home.yml Save personal destinations and return to them across servers. Command Purpose Default permission /home [name] Travel to your home; player.name selects another owner's home. sparrow.command.home[.other] /set_home [name] Create a home at your position; the default name is home. sparrow.command.set_home /del_home <name> Delete a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.del_home[.other] /home_list [owner|page] [page] List your homes or another owner's homes. sparrow.command.home_list[.other] /edit_home <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.edit_home[.other] /sparrow del_all_homes [--player <player>] [--server <server>] [--world <world>] Bulk delete from console; at least one filter, no confirmation. sparrow.command.del_all_homes /set_home mine /home mine /home Steve.mine /home_list Steve 2 Without a name, /home prefers default-name, then your only home. /set_home does not overwrite an existing name. Use player.name to visit, delete or edit another owner's home, with the corresponding .other permission. home_list takes the owner's name directly. The rename and relocate branches of edit_home also need .rename and .relocate. del_all_homes is console-only and deletes immediately using the intersection of all supplied filters. The default limit is 3 homes. sparrow.home.limit.<amount> overrides max-homes; sparrow.home.limit.unlimited removes the limit. See Teleport options for teleport behavior. With PlaceholderAPI installed, use sparrowhome_count, sparrowhome_limit, sparrowhome_remaining and sparrowhome_list. In Sparrow text, write <papi:sparrowhome_count>. Unlimited limits and remaining counts return -1.

Module maintenance · Configuration features/maintenance.yml Block ordinary players from joining during maintenance and show a BossBar to online players. Command Purpose Default permission /maintenance [true|false] [--all] [--tag <tag>] Change maintenance mode. sparrow.command.maintenance /maintenance true /maintenance false --all /maintenance true --tag survival With no arguments, toggle maintenance on this server; use true or false to set it explicitly. --all targets online network servers; --tag selects servers by tag. sparrow.bypass.maintenance allows entry during maintenance. active stores the maintenance state. boss-bar.enabled controls the bar; its color and style are configured under boss-bar.

Module patrol · Configuration features/patrol.yml Cycle through players across the network by teleporting to them. Omit the target to rotate through eligible players. Command Purpose Default permission /patrol [targets] Cycle through players for patrol, including across servers. sparrow.command.patrol sparrow.bypass.patrol excludes a player. Spectators are skipped by default; set skip-spectators: false to include them.

Module player_limit · Configuration features/player_limit.yml Change this server's player limit at runtime. Command changes are saved. Command Purpose Default permission /max_players [amount] View or change the player limit; -1 restores the original limit. sparrow.command.max_players sparrow.bypass.player_limit allows joining when full. max-players: -1 restores the limit from before the module was enabled; 0 sets a zero-player limit. Disabling the module also restores the original limit.

Module quick-shulker · Configuration features/quick-shulker.yml Hold a shulker box and sneak-right-click the air to open it. The off hand is supported; the main hand takes priority. No command or separate usage permission is required. require-sneaking: true allow-offhand: true title: '<arg:hover_name>' disabled-worlds: [] <arg:hover_name> uses the box's item name. List restricted worlds in disabled-worlds.

Module rtp · Configuration features/rtp.yml Find a safe location within a region, including on another backend. The traveler must be on this server. Command Purpose Default permission /rtp <player> <region> [--silent] Teleport randomly within a configured region. sparrow.command.rtp[.other] /rtp_range <player> <server> <world> <min-radius> <max-radius> [options] Teleport randomly within a specified square range. sparrow.command.rtp_range[.other] regions: wild: server: survival permission: sparrow.rtp.wild area: world: - x: [-5000, 5000] z: [-5000, 5000] /rtp Steve wild /rtp_range Steve survival world 500 5000 --center-x 0 --center-z 0 Omit server to use this server; omit permission for unrestricted region access. A region can contain multiple worlds and rectangles. Add y: [60, 120] to a rectangle to limit feet height. rtp_range uses a square ring, or a full square when the minimum radius is 0. The center defaults to (0, 0); provide --min-y and --max-y together. Both commands share the RTP cooldown and accept --silent / -s. See Teleport options for cooldowns and warmups, and Landing rules for destination selection.

Module spawn · Configuration features/spawn.yml Travel to the configured spawn, including on another backend. The command is unavailable until a destination is configured. Command Purpose Default permission /spawn Travel to the configured spawn. sparrow.command.spawn destination: server: lobby world: world x: 0.5 y: 64 z: 0.5 yaw: 0 pitch: 0 teleport-options: cooldown: 5m warmup: duration: 0s Configure the destination on each server and run /spr reload. Spawn uses the exact coordinates without a safe-location search. Spawn supports cooldowns, warmups and permission overrides. Its warmup fields use hyphens, such as cancel-on-move and cancel-on-damage.

Module tpa · Configuration features/tpa.yml Send, accept or decline player-to-player teleport requests across servers. Command Purpose Default permission /tpa <player> Ask to teleport to another player. sparrow.command.tpa /tpa_here <player> Ask another player to teleport to you. sparrow.command.tpa_here /tpa_accept [player] Accept a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_accept /tpa_deny [player] Deny a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_deny /tpa_cancel [player] Cancel an outgoing request; omit the player to cancel all. sparrow.command.tpa_cancel expire-seconds: 60 request-cooldown-seconds: 10 deny-cooldown-seconds: 120 Requests expire after 60 seconds by default, with 10 seconds between requests and 120 seconds before requesting the same player after a denial. sparrow.bypass.tpa_cooldown skips both request cooldowns. After acceptance, teleport-options applies to the actual traveler. Its teleport cooldown is separate from request intervals; see Teleport options.

Module warp · Configuration features/warp.yml Named destinations shared across your Sparrow servers. Command Purpose Default permission /warp <name> [player] Travel to a warp, with support for cross-server players. sparrow.command.warp[.other] /set_warp <name> Create a warp at your position. sparrow.command.set_warp /del_warp <name> Delete a warp. sparrow.command.del_warp /warp_list [page] List warps. sparrow.command.warp_list /edit_warp <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a warp. sparrow.command.edit_warp /set_warp market /warp market /edit_warp market relocate Creation and relocation require a player. /set_warp does not overwrite an existing name. Names allow up to 32 characters; the default pattern accepts letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. rename and relocate additionally require sparrow.command.edit_warp.rename and sparrow.command.edit_warp.relocate. Use /del_warp to delete a warp. With permission-restrict enabled, viewing and using a warp requires sparrow.warp.use.<lowercase-name>. Management still uses command permissions. Configure cooldowns, warmups and arrival effects under teleport-options; see Teleport options.

Cooldowns, warmups and arrival effects are configured in each feature's own file. For example, in features/home.yml: teleport-options: cooldown: 5m warmup: duration: 5s cancel_on_move: true cancel_on_damage: true display: action_bar invulnerability: 5s after_sound: entity.enderman.teleport overrides: - permission: sparrow.home.teleport.staff cooldown: 0s warmup: duration: 0s - permission: sparrow.home.teleport.vip cooldown: 1m warmup: duration: 3s Option Meaning cooldown Cross-server cooldown starting after a successful teleport; 0s disables it. warmup.duration Wait before departure; 0s teleports immediately. cancel_on_move / cancel_on_damage Cancel the countdown after moving over half a block, changing worlds or taking damage. display action_bar, title, boss_bar, chat or none. invulnerability Protection duration after arrival. after_sound Arrival sound; an empty string or zero volume disables it. overrides Select the first matching traveler permission. Omitted options inherit; a supplied warmup replaces the entire option. Warmups also accept boss_bar_color, boss_bar_overlay, warmup_sound and cancel_sound. Sounds accept a name or name,volume,pitch, such as entity.enderman.teleport,0.5,1.

Feature Configuration location Home, Warp, TPA, RTP teleport-options in their respective features/<feature>.yml. Back, DeathBack back.teleport-options and deathback.teleport-options in features/back.yaml. Spawn teleport-options in features/spawn.yml; supports only cooldowns, warmups and permission overrides. Spawn uses hyphenated warmup fields, such as cancel-on-move and boss-bar-color, and defaults to a 0s warmup. The other features above default to a 5m cooldown, 5s warmup and 5s arrival protection. Cooldowns are separate per feature, including separate Back and DeathBack cooldowns. See Landing rules for destination selection.

Each feature defines how it chooses a landing position. Feature Destination selection Spawn, Home, Warp, offline teleport Saved or configured coordinates. TPA, patrol The target player's position. Back, DeathBack Check the original coordinates, then search within 4 blocks horizontally and 8 blocks up or down. RTP Search randomly within the configured region; surface scanning in ordinary worlds, cavity scanning in ceiling dimensions such as the Nether. World Check the destination, then search within 8 blocks horizontally and 16 blocks up or down if needed. Safety searches check boundaries, collisions, support and hazardous blocks. Back, DeathBack and RTP reject water, leaf support and Nether-roof locations by default. World allows shallow water with the head above the surface. For Back, DeathBack and World, --unsafe allows the original coordinates if the search fails. RTP ends without teleporting when it cannot find a safe location. There is no general YAML processor list for changing these rules. Developers can combine search rules and processors through the Teleport API.
